title: Impact of Surprise Electoral Outcomes on Industry Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology is appropriate here. The surprise electoral outcome serves as an exogenous shock that allows us to measure abnormal returns around the event date (day 0). The key assumption is that in the absence of the election event, stock returns would follow their normal relationship with market returns as captured by the market model. We'll calculate abnormal returns as the difference between actual returns and expected returns based on each industry's beta.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s64_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns using market model
data <- data %>%
  mutate(abnormal_return = ret - beta * mkt_ret)

# Define event windows
estimation_window <- data %>% filter(event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -2)
event_window <- data %>% filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 3)
post_event <- data %>% filter(event_day >= 1 & event_day <= 3)

# Calculate Cumulative Abnormal Returns (CAR) for each stock
car_results <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(
    car_pre = sum(abnormal_return[event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 0]),
    car_post = sum(abnormal_return[event_day >= 1 & event_day <= 3]),
    car_full = sum(abnormal_return[event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 3]),
    beta = first(beta),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Main analysis: Test if CAR is significantly different from zero
cat("=== EVENT STUDY RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Sample size:", nrow(car_results), "industries\n\n")

# Test CAR around event (days -1 to +3)
t_test_full <- t.test(car_results$car_full, mu = 0)
cat("CAR [-1, +3] Results:\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", round(mean(car_results$car_full), 4), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_test_full$statistic, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(t_test_full$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(t_test_full$conf.int[1], 4), ",", round(t_test_full$conf.int[2], 4), "]\n\n")

# Test post-event CAR (days +1 to +3)
t_test_post <- t.test(car_results$car_post, mu = 0)
cat("CAR [+1, +3] Results:\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", round(mean(car_results$car_post), 4), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_test_post$statistic, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(t_test_post$p.value, 4), "\n\n")

# Robustness check 1: Test by beta quartiles
car_results$beta_quartile <- ntile(car_results$beta, 4)
cat("=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK: BY BETA QUARTILES ===\n")
beta_analysis <- car_results %>%
  group_by(beta_quartile) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_car = mean(car_full),
    t_stat = t.test(car_full, mu = 0)$statistic,
    p_value = t.test(car_full, mu = 0)$p.value,
    n = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )
print(beta_analysis)

# Robustness check 2: Alternative event window [-2, +2]
car_alt <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car_alt = sum(abnormal_return[event_day >= -2 & event_day <= 2]), .groups = 'drop')

t_test_alt <- t.test(car_alt$car_alt, mu = 0)
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK: ALTERNATIVE WINDOW [-2, +2] ===\n")
cat("Mean CAR:", round(mean(car_alt$car_alt), 4), "\n")
cat("t-statistic:", round(t_test_alt$statistic, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value:", round(t_test_alt$p.value, 4), "\n")

# Summary statistics
cat("\n=== SUMMARY STATISTICS ===\n")
cat("Standard deviation of CAR:", round(sd(car_results$car_full), 4), "\n")
cat("Percentage of positive CARs:", round(mean(car_results$car_full > 0) * 100, 1), "%\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect to find small but statistically significant negative cumulative abnormal returns in the range of -1% to -3% over the event window. Surprise electoral outcomes typically create uncertainty and market volatility, leading to temporary negative reactions as investors reassess risk premiums. Industries with higher betas (more sensitive to market movements) should show larger absolute abnormal returns. The effect should be most pronounced in the immediate post-event period (days +1 to +3) as markets digest the unexpected information and adjust expectations about future policy implications.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Analyze stock returns before and after the election event to isolate the impact of the surprise outcome.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The unexpected election result led to a negative impact on industry-level CAR.
